entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8761"/><div sID="gen14536" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8761"/>5. Translate, "As the heat in a dry land (is brought down by the shadow of a cloud, so) thou shalt bring down the tumult (the shout of triumph over their enemies) of strangers (foreigners); and as the heat by the shadow of the cloud (is brought low), so the branch (the offspring) of the terrible ones shall be brought low." Parkhurst translates the Hebrew for "branch," the exulting song. Jerome translates the last clause, "And as when the heat burns under a cloud, thou shalt make the branch of the terrible ones to wither"; the branch withering even under the friendly shade of a cloud typifies the wicked brought to ruin, not for want of natural means of prosperity, but by the immediate act of God. <div eID="gen14536" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8763"/><div sID="gen14544" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8763"/><hi type="bold">7. face of ... covering--</hi>image from mourning, in which it was usual to cover the face with a veil (<reference osisRef="2Sam.15.30">2Sa 15:30</reference>). "Face of covering," that is, the covering itself; as in <reference osisRef="Job.41.13">Job 41:13</reference>, "the face of his garment," the garment itself. The covering or veil is the mist of ignorance as to a future state, and the way to eternal life, which enveloped the nations (<reference osisRef="Eph.4.18">Ep 4:18</reference>) and the unbelieving Jew (<reference osisRef="2Cor.3.15">2Co 3:15</reference>). The Jew, however, is first to be converted before the conversion of "all nations"; for it is "in this mountain," namely, Zion, that the latter are to have the veil taken off (<reference osisRef="Ps.102.13">Psa 102:13</reference>, 15, 16, 21, 22; <reference osisRef="Rom.11.12">Ro 11:12</reference>). <div eID="gen14544" type="x-p"/>

And it shall be said in that day, &c.--</hi>"After death has been swallowed up for ever, the people of God, who had been delivered from the hand of death, shall say to the Lord, Lo, this is our God, whom unbelievers regarded as only a man" [Jerome]. "The words are so moulded as to point us specially to the person of the Son of God, who 'saves' us; as He vouchsafed to Israel temporal saving, so to His elect He appears for the purpose of conferring eternal salvation" [Vitringa]. And it shall be said in that day, &c.-- "After death has been swallowed up for ever, the people of God, who had been delivered from the hand of death, shall say to the Lord, Lo, this is our God, whom unbelievers regarded as only a man" [Jerome]. "The words are so moulded as to point us specially to the person of the Son of God, who 'saves' us; as He vouchsafed to Israel temporal saving, so to His elect He appears for the purpose of conferring eternal salvation" [Vitringa]. The Jews, however, have a special share in the words, This is our God (see on Is 25:6 ). we have waited-- "Waited" is characteristic of God's people in all ages ( Ge 49:18 ; Tit 2:13 ). we will be glad and rejoice in his salvation-- compare Psa 118:24 , which refers to the second coming of Jesus (compare Psa 118:26 , with Lu 13:35 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8767"/><div sID="gen14555" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8767"/><hi type="bold">11. he--</hi>Jehovah shall spread His hands to strike the foe on this side and on that, with as little effort as a swimmer spreads forth his arms to cleave a passage through the water [Calvin]. (<reference osisRef="Zech.5.3">Zec 5:3</reference>). Lowth takes "he" as Moab, who, in danger of sinking, shall strain every nerve to save himself; but Jehovah (and "he") shall cause him to sink ("bring down the pride" of Moab, <reference osisRef="Isa.16.6">Is 16:6</reference>).<div eID="gen14555" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14556" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">with the spoils of ... hands--</hi>literally, "the craftily acquired spoils" of his (Moab's) hands [Barnes]. Moab's pride, as well as the sudden gripe of his hands (namely, whereby he tries to save himself from drowning) [Lowth]. "Together with the joints of his hands," that is, though Moab struggle against Jehovah hand and foot [Maurer]. <div eID="gen14556" type="x-p"/>

entries.reader_content_plain: 11. he-- Jehovah shall spread His hands to strike the foe on this side and on that, with as little effort as a swimmer spreads forth his arms to cleave a passage through the water [Calvin]. ( Zec 5:3 ). Lowth takes "he" as Moab, who, in danger of sinking, shall strain every nerve to save himself; but Jehovah (and "he") shall cause him to sink ("bring down the pride" of Moab, Is 16:6 ). with the spoils of ... hands-- literally, "the craftily acquired spoils" of his (Moab's) hands [Barnes]. Moab's pride, as well as the sudden gripe of his hands (namely, whereby he tries to save himself from drowning) [Lowth]. "Together with the joints of his hands," that is, though Moab struggle against Jehovah hand and foot [Maurer].
